claims.text: The starting HfMoTaTiZr alloy is an approximately equiatomic alloy containing 20 at.% of each element.
As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has a density of approximately 10.21 g/cm³.
As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has high strength at room temperature and around 1000 °C.
As-cast HfMoTaTiZr is a disordered, single-phase BCC solid solution.
The proposed intervention produces nominal Hf0.5Nb0.3V0.2MoTaTiZr by replacing half of the original Hf content with Nb and V.
Replacing part of the heavy Hf with lighter Nb and V reduces the alloy's bulk density.
The proposed substitution will reduce density by approximately 8–12% relative to as-cast HfMoTaTiZr.
Hf0.5Nb0.3V0.2MoTaTiZr will remain a uniform, single-phase BCC solid solution.
Residual Hf together with the selected Nb/V ratio will maintain substantial atomic-size mismatch and lattice distortion.
Maintained lattice distortion will preserve strong solid-solution strengthening.
The refractory elemental mixture will preserve high-temperature stability near 1000 °C.
The modified alloy will retain yield strength comparable to the baseline at room temperature.
The modified alloy will retain yield strength comparable to the baseline near 1000 °C.
The modified alloy will retain creep resistance comparable to HfMoTaTiZr at room temperature and near 1000 °C.
Arc melting followed by homogenization at about 1150 °C for one hour will ensure uniform elemental distribution.
The proposed performance window extends from room temperature to approximately 1000 °C under quasi-static tensile and creep loading in a protective atmosphere.
Secondary-phase formation or a yield-strength loss exceeding approximately 10% lies outside the acceptable performance boundary.
Refractory HEAs commonly possess BCC solid solutions with high-temperature strength and thermal stability.
Distorted lattices and the high melting temperatures of refractory constituent elements are associated with elevated-temperature mechanical performance in refractory HEAs.
The optimum Nb/V ratio and the resulting balance among phase stability, density, and strengthening remain uncertain and require compositional optimization.

contradictions.description: The formula Hf0.5Nb0.3V0.2MoTaTiZr corresponds to approximately Hf 10 at.%, Nb 6 at.%, and V 4 at.% after normalization, whereas the intervention describes Nb as 30% and V as 20% of the overall alloy composition. Those overall percentages are incompatible with the stated formula and with reducing Hf to half of its original equiatomic fraction.
